intro: The grooved flow distributor is the quiet workhorse here. It's built into the piston specifically to keep pressure drop nearly zero as flow moves through, which is what lets a medium-pressure column still deliver good separation efficiency.

Swelling compensation solves a real, specific problem. Soft polymer sorbents change volume as the mobile phase changes, and without correction, that shift either loosens the bed or over-compresses it. The optional software application moves the piston in very small steps up and down to track that change automatically.
Sealing is handled differently than on PC01. UHMWPE pistons here come with integral sealing wings built into the piston itself, rather than separate sealing rings.
Frit pore size is larger than PC01's. 5 microns here versus 3 microns on the high-pressure line, fixed with a simple stainless steel ring rather than a removable frit ring assembly.
The stand is included on every column, not conditional on diameter the way PC01's is.
Two related variants exist within the confirmed range. PC01 (high-pressure) and PC04 (non-metal), both cross-referenced directly by ECOM's own page.

intro: The whole column body is UHMWPE, not just the piston seals the way it is on PC01 or PC02. Nothing in the flow path is metal, which is exactly what biochromatography and other sensitive applications require.

Piston actuation comes in two forms. Type A moves the input piston with flange bolts. Type B uses a central stainless steel threaded rod instead, which sits outside the mobile phase and doesn't compromise the non-metal contact claim.

Frits are polypropylene here, not stainless steel mesh, at 10 micron pore size, coarser than PC01's 3 microns or PC02's 5 microns. That coarser frit matches the lower pressure ceiling a plastic column is built to handle.
Pressure runs lower than either metal line. 16 bar down to 5 bar across the confirmed range, well below PC02's 15 to 50 bar and far below PC01's 80 to 200 bar.
One discrepancy in the source data is worth noting directly. The column labeled PC04-25/250 lists an inner diameter of 50 mm, not 25 mm, in its own configuration data.
Two related variants exist within the confirmed range. PC01 (high-pressure) and PC02 (medium-pressure), both cross-referenced directly by ECOM's own page.
